model.name: Dangling tree links — a user clicks a chevron/link and it expands to EMPTY @390
model.description: USER-VISIBLE DEFECT (architect prod sweep, served v0.8.150). A forward ref in the trace/model tree points to a unit that does NOT exist, so when a user taps the chevron or link it expands to EMPTY — a dead click. MEASURED: architect 41 dangling forward refs ON THE SERVED TREE (the user-facing number); robbin-req measured 469 on the working tree (dirtier — uncommitted peer churn/branch-diff), so the SERVED 41 is authoritative for what a user hits (measure-honesty: served != working). Sibling of R37.29 referential-integrity (a ref that does not resolve), surfaced here as the USER symptom.

discoverySource.note: PO delivery-first capture (LAW 2): user-visible @390 defect, screenshot-checkable AC. Fix ships in parallel; capture does not block delivery.

model.crossRefNote: Surfaces the user-visible face of the traceability-integrity family (R37.29 referential-integrity / R37.32 forward-authoritative). Same root, but stated in what the USER SEES @390, not model contents.
model.satisfactionStatus: UNVERIFIED — OPEN DEFECT on served v0.8.150; fix ships (expert), Tron prioritizes; screenshot-@390 verifies.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On 390px, tapping any visible chevron/link expands to REAL content, never a blank/empty node. Screenshot: no expanded node is empty.

A forward ref whose target does not exist is NOT shown as a clickable chevron (hidden or shown disabled-with-reason), so a user cannot dead-click into emptiness. Screenshot: no live chevron yields nothing.
The served-tree dangling-forward-ref count (architect baseline 41) trends to 0; the gate measures the SERVED build, not a fixture.
